data.narrative:
Core Automation, a stealth-stage AI & Software company founded by Gerald Depew and Daniel C. Rozok, is targeting a Series funding round of $500M–$1B at a $4–5B+ valuation. The relevant comp universe spans AI & Software, encompassing 1 public comparable (Palantir, PLTR) and 8 private peers including Palantir, Waymo, Figure AI, Scale AI, and Reflection AI.

Peer-median valuation proves inapplicable here. Despite 16 same-sector peers existing in AI & Software, none met the filtering criteria for stage alignment, adjacent-stage proximity, or similar valuation tier—each threshold required a minimum of three datapoints to be analytically defensible. Relying on all-sector median multiples would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of business models, revenue maturity, and capital intensity across the broader AI & Software landscape.

The absence of tight comparables at the stealth stage within this sector reflects a structural gap in the data rather than analytical failure. Without sufficient peer granularity to support quantitative triangulation, this valuation cannot be anchored to empirical multiples. The stated target range of $4–5B+ should be treated as a directional signal from the capital markets rather than a conclusion derived from comparable-company analysis. Further clarity on Core Automation's revenue stage, customer traction, and capital efficiency would be necessary to establish a defensible valuation range.
